title: Metrizable profinite quotients through which a metric-valued function factors
statement: Let $S$ be a profinite space (compact Hausdorff with a basis of clopen sets), let $G$ be a profinite group (compact Hausdorff with a basis of open normal subgroups), let $r\geq1$ be an integer, and let $(Y,d_Y)$ be a metric space, with no completeness hypothesis. For every continuous $f:S\times G^r\to Y$ there exist a metrizable profinite space $S_0$, a metrizable profinite group $G_0$, continuous surjections $p:S\to S_0$ and $q:G\to G_0$, with $q$ a group homomorphism, and a continuous $f_0:S_0\times G_0^r\to Y$ such that $f=f_0\circ(p\times q^r)$. The empty $S$ is allowed. All spaces use [def-weil-size-convention].

source.place: Paragraph (3), scalar tame-kernel expansion: metrizable reduction of one continuous cocycle, without completing its values; agent-formulated auxiliary lemma, exact literature reference WANTED.

proof.text: The clopen sets form a basis on the profinite space S by Mathlib isTopologicalBasis_isClopen. Every identity neighbourhood in G contains an open identity neighbourhood, which contains an open normal subgroup by ProfiniteGrp.exist_openNormalSubgroup_sub_open_nhds_of_one. These provide the hypotheses of the finite oscillation lemma, also when S is empty.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent metrizable reduction: sequence of finite rectangular quotients

proof.text: For every natural n apply [lem-sfb-profinite-product-finite-oscillation] with epsilon 1/(n+1)>0. Choose its finite partition P_n, open normal subgroup N_n, and part map p_n. Give A_n=P_n the discrete topology and B_n=G/N_n its quotient topology, which the lemma proves discrete and finite. The quotient group homomorphisms q_n and part maps p_n are continuous, and equality of their coordinates gives distance of f-values less than 1/(n+1). This construction already covers empty S.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent metrizable reduction: sequence of finite rectangular quotients

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-countable-finite-coordinate-images] to p_n and q_n. Equip their explicitly constructed diagonal images S_0=range(s -> (p_n(s))_n) and G_0=range(g -> (q_n(g))_n) with the supplied compact, Hausdorff, totally disconnected and metrizable structures. Bundle these as Profinite and ProfiniteGrp. Their range corestrictions p and q are continuous surjections and q is a homomorphism. Equality under p or q is equivalent to equality in every finite coordinate. The products and subtypes stay in the original universe [def-weil-size-convention].

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent metrizable reduction: metrizable profinite diagonal images

proof.text: Define the continuous product map R(s,g)=(p(s),(q(g_i))_i). If R(x)=R(xprime), the coordinate equality assertions give equality under p_n and q_n for every n. Thus dist(f(x),f(xprime))<1/(n+1) for all n. A strictly positive distance would exceed 1/(n+1) for some n by exists_nat_one_div_lt, a contradiction. The distance is zero, so metric separation gives equality in Y.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent metrizable reduction: fibre constancy in the original metric target

proof.text: The map R is onto by choosing one preimage under p and a preimage under q independently in each group coordinate. Its domain is compact, using [lem-weil-pbc-tychonoff-product-quasi-compact] for the finite power of G and product compactness with S. The target is Hausdorff. Apply [lem-sfb-compact-hausdorff-surjection-quotient], namely Topology.IsQuotientMap.of_surjective_continuous, to R.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent metrizable reduction: quotient topology of the product surjection

proof.text: Use Topology.IsQuotientMap.lift to descend the continuous f, which step 4 proves constant on R-fibres. This gives a continuous map f_0 into Y itself, even when S and Y are empty. The lift_comp identity evaluated at x gives f(x)=f_0(R(x)). No completion or choice of an unspecified data object from an unproved existence theorem is used: both quotient spaces are the concrete diagonal images of step 3.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent metrizable reduction: continuous descent and universes
